summary: Implement only not.b32 and cnot.b32 over all 32-bit inputs using the shared pure-instruction rules.
Preserve incoming operand values under aliasing, guarded execution, exact operand reads and the restricted typed frontend.
Separate checked result and execution proofs from PTX source fidelity and hardware correspondence.
remaining: The selected typed .b32 forms and their shared-engine proofs are implemented. Other widths, predicate-valued forms, raw-module validation, whole-kernel execution and hardware correspondence remain separate obligations.

from.quote:
The typed frontend accepts exactly the selected spellings and word operand shapes.
A malformed use of a recognized spelling is distinguished from an unsupported
spelling. Register declarations and immediate conversion have already been
checked by the caller: a word literal is a decoded 32-bit value, not arbitrary
raw PTX text. Other widths, predicate-valued forms and raw module parsing remain
outside the family.

passage.quote:
def decode (statement : Scalar.Text.Statement) : Except Scalar.Text.DecodeError Instr :=
  if statement.mnemonic = "not.b32" then
    match statement.operands with
    | [.word (.reg d), .word a] => .ok ⟨statement.guard, .bitNot, d, a⟩
    | _ => .error (.invalidOperands statement.mnemonic)
  else if statement.mnemonic = "cnot.b32" then
    match statement.operands with
    | [.word (.reg d), .word a] => .ok ⟨statement.guard, .cnot, d, a⟩
    | _ => .error (.invalidOperands statement.mnemonic)
  else .error (.unsupportedMnemonic statement.mnemonic)

from.quote:
This family implements only not.b32 and cnot.b32. Bitwise not flips all 32 source bits. Logical cnot returns the word one exactly when the whole source word is zero, and returns zero otherwise.
All 32-bit words are admitted, including zero and values with the highest bit set.
No interpretation as a signed integer or floating-point number changes these bits.

passage.quote:
def compute (op : Operation) (a : Word) : Word :=
  match op with
  | .bitNot => ~~~a
  | .cnot => if a = 0 then 1 else 0

from.quote:
Proofs establish the exact result, preserved state, determinism, one-step
existence and origin in the fetched program.

passage.quote:
theorem step_exists (target : Ptx.Target) (program : List Instr) (s : Scalar.State) (i : Instr)
    (supported : SupportedTarget target) (fetch : program[s.pc]? = some i) :
    ∃ next event, Step target program s next event := by
  have mapped : (program.map lower)[s.pc]? = some (lower i) := by simp [fetch]
  apply Pure32.step_exists (target := target) (program := program.map lower) (i := lower i)
    (s := s) (fetch := mapped)
  exact supported
